operation.access_schedule: Interaction follows the sequence in registry.protocols. Current loss feedback is available only after the action is submitted. Any pre-action disclosure of context or advice is specified separately.
operation.coupling: Each call draws a fresh independent sample. The noise $Z_t$ is independent of the pre-action history and private randomness. Neither the optimal static allocation nor $\mu$ or the gaps is supplied. Recommendation follows exhaustion of the budget; stopping-time optimization and cumulative regret are not the task.

bindings.source_value: Private randomization is allowed. The seed is hidden from the environment and independent of the fixed instance and sample randomness.

After at most $T$ samples, return a recommended arm $\widehat{b}_T\in[K]$. Any postprocessing of the observed history is allowed. The arm need not have been sampled, and no additional certificate is required.
Only the stated statistical guarantee is required, not a certificate verifiable through the feedback interface.
Retain the native objective and complete resource vector. At fixed $T$, compare cumulative regret. Best-arm-identification stopping times and error probabilities use their own task-specific criteria.

The mean μ_i belongs to the ith fixed reward distribution. It is unknown and cannot be queried directly.

$H_{\mathrm{so}}(\mu)^{-1}=\sup_{w\in\Delta_K^\circ}\inf_{\lambda\in\operatorname{Alt}(\mu)}\sum_i w_i\,\operatorname{KL}(\mathcal N(\lambda_i,1)\|\mathcal N(\mu_i,1))$. This is an analytical benchmark only.

protocols.adversary_information: The unknown distribution or parameter is fixed before interaction. Learner randomness and sample randomness are independent. No adversary changes the distribution round by round from the learner's history.
protocols.loss_bearing_points: There is no regret loss. Only T identification samples are counted.
protocols.past_requery: No new information may be requested from past rounds or previously used samples. Received feedback may be stored and processed. In a stochastic model, an action may be repeated in a new round, with a fresh charged sample.
protocols.queries_per_round: For each budget T, the algorithm takes exactly T samples. The comparison concerns relative error-exponent difficulty as T → ∞.
steps: Fix mu; A_T receives public K, T, and variance one.
Choose arms from the history and receive Gaussian samples sequentially until exactly $T$ samples have been taken.
Return a recommendation and define its error probability p_{μ,T}.
First take the limsup as T tends to infinity for fixed mu, then the supremum over mu, and finally the infimum over uniform algorithm families.
